as_told.title: John McCarthy's Stanford AI lab story of the Bureau of Simulation replacing a predictable man

plain: John McCarthy, who ran the artificial intelligence lab "on the hill" at Stanford, used to tell a story: one day you get a letter from the "Bureau of Simulation" that begins "Dear Sir," and says a man as predictable as you can be replaced by a simulation. The researcher Jacques Vallée tells Michels he heard McCarthy tell it, around 1968 in one telling and only "in the early AI era" in the other. The point of the story is that if a person's behaviour can be predicted, a machine could stand in for him.
